## Ticket proposals
- **collab: a take recorded during a wrap can be refused and lost** — suggested P1; open, with Spud.
  Why: The membership gate completes an abandoned wrap on READ (collab/index.ts:655-674), mutating the in-memory collab row to status='wrapped' before any mode is dispatched. commit's own phase gate then refuses, because writablePhase() does not admit 'wrapped'. So the first take committed after the last hot seat stops recording is answered 403 closed and its row is never written — even though the member already uploaded the bytes through a signed URL, and even though the whole point of the 'wrapping' phase is that whoever is mid-part finishes. The same interaction makes commit's own wrap-completion copy (index.ts:1128-1145) unreachable outside a sub-millisecond race: whenever it would fire, the gate has already fired. BAD-047 must not change this in the split (the spike's risk 9 says leave both copies alone), so it needs a decision of its own.
  Evidence: Pinned live in test/server/functions.test.mjs, 'collab: a wrapping room finishes on the next member read, and the take after that is refused' — against a local stack: heartbeat recording:false leaves status 'wrapping' (the beat is judged while the seat is still hot), the next info reads phase 'wrapped', and the next commit answers 403 {error:'closed',code:'closed'} with collab_takes still holding 2 rows. Reproduced independently by a throwaway probe before the test was written.
- **collab: join answers one reason with two status codes** — suggested P3; open, with Spud.
  Why: A join code that does not normalize (normalizeJoinCode returns null) answers 404 {allowed:false, reason:'unknown_code'}; a code that normalizes fine but names no room falls through to decideJoin and answers 403 with the SAME body. Same word, two statuses, decided by a detail the person typing has no way to see. Clients branch on data.code || data.error and on the join shape's reason, so nothing is broken today, but any client or proxy that keys on status treats one typo as 'not found' and the next as 'forbidden'. Worth settling deliberately rather than inheriting it through the BAD-047 split, where one of the two is easy to normalize away by accident.
  Evidence: collab/index.ts:430 (the 404) and :469's decideJoin path (the 403); _shared/collab.mjs decideJoin returns reason 'unknown_code' for a null collab. Both pinned in test/server/functions.test.mjs, 'collab: join names an unknown code two ways, and a rejoin is the same seat': 'not a code' -> 404, 'BT-ZZZZZZ' -> 403, identical bodies.
- **collab: upload-url reports a missing or zero byte count as *_too_large** — suggested P3; open, with Spud.
  Why: upload-url's size check is one expression — Number.isFinite(bytes) && bytes > 0 && bytes <= MAX — and every way of failing it answers the same code: bytes:0, bytes:-1, bytes:'lots' and a body with no bytes at all all come back 413 {code:'thumb_too_large'|'scene_too_large'|'take_too_large', max}. A client told 'too large' for a value that is nothing of the kind will show the wrong copy and may retry by shrinking something that was never the problem. A distinct 400 bad_bytes for the not-a-positive-number half would cost one branch per kind and say what actually happened.
  Evidence: collab/index.ts:985-988 (thumb), :999-1002 (scene), :1010-1013 (take), :1019-1022 (cam). Pinned in test/server/functions.test.mjs, 'collab: upload-url refuses before it ever signs': bytes of 0, -1, 'lots' and null all answer 413 thumb_too_large against a local stack.
